newsitem.title: RUSSIA: U.S. rating agency positive on Russia - minister.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rating agency positive on Russia - minister.

text.p: The U.S. rating agency preparing a credit rating for Russia's first Eurobond has a positive impression of Russia, but hopes expressed by some officials Russia will get a rating similar to Spain are over-optimistic, a senior finance ministry official said on Wednesday.
Economy Minister Yevgeny Yasin said on Tuesday that Russia may get a rating similar to Greece, Spain or Portugal.
"As for Spain, that's too optimistic," deputy finance minister Oleg Vyugin, who is making regular reports to the agency now in Moscow, told Reuters.
Yasin met the agency on Tuesday.
Officials declined to identify the agency now in Moscow. But Western bankers said it was Standard and Poors.
It is the second agency to come to Moscow to draw up a rating for the Eurobond issue planned to be launched by the end of September or early October.
Vyugin previously said the rating would be ready and published by the end of September.
Western bankers said they expected Russia to receive a BBB or BB rating -- just above or just below investment grade, but the Eurobond would in any case attract great interest.
Finance ministry officials declined to comment on acceptances for Russia's $35 billion debt rescheduling deal with its commercial bank creditors in the London Club.
Banks signing up to the deal, which was agreed to last year, had to do so by August 27. Acceptances involving a "critical mass" of $20 billion were needed for the deal to go ahead.
Bankers said reconciling the claims on more than 3,000 individual loans from around 600 banks was time-consuming, and it could be several weeks before results of the acceptance process were known.
